rv.q: It’s hard for me to say that “The Fever” is a jolly time in the theater, but it is darned effective.
Ferguson makes the most of it, delivering a wonderfully entertaining portrayal that benefits greatly from the close proximity of the audience numbering less than a hundred.
Allen's script sags near the end, weighed down by wheel-spinning biographical exposition...and the failure to arrive of a satisfying climax.
Spending an afternoon with this Capote is something you wouldn’t wish on his worst enemies
